title: Using super without an explicit superclass
answer: Every ordinary Java class that does not explicitly extend another class implicitly extends `java.lang.Object`. Therefore `super()` in such a class refers to Object's constructor, and inherited Object methods are available. You cannot use `super` from `Object` itself because Object has no superclass. The rule explains why even a simple class with no `extends` clause participates in a superclass chain.
